title: Copilot Studio: persistent identity (agent accounts) for agents
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts and the documented Frontier preview behaviour support its claims. The two admin switches, corrected agent-blocking path, beta Graph call, licensing requirements and shared-memory warnings are supported by Microsoft Learn.

claims.claim: Agent accounts are admin-opt-in: admins must activate the template and enable the environment setting before users can create them.
claims.quote: An admin completed both steps to turn on agent accounts: activate the Copilot Studio agent template in the Microsoft 365 admin center and turn on Agent accounts for your environment in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Only selected users and members of selected groups can create agents with accounts.
claims.quote: Only the users you select at this step and members of the selected groups can create agents with accounts.

claims.claim: The feature page assigns template activation to a tenant admin.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, a tenant admin goes to All Agents, filters by Agent template: Yes, selects Copilot Studio (Frontier), and then selects Activate.

claims.claim: Template activation uses Microsoft 365 admin center > All Agents > filter Agent template: Yes > Copilot Studio (Frontier) > Activate > Users step.
claims.quote:
a tenant admin goes to All Agents, filters by Agent template: Yes, selects Copilot Studio (Frontier), and then selects Activate.

claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio (Frontier)" template activate Microsoft Graph API PowerShell; "Copilot Studio" "template" "activation" "copilotPackage"; "copilotPackage" "activate". Opened the account guide and copilotPackage resource reference; neither documents this activation call.

claims.claim: The environment setting is at Power Platform admin center > Copilot > Settings > Copilot Studio > Agent accounts.
claims.quote:
select Copilot on the side bar, and then select Settings. The Settings page appears.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationales: risk, impact
claims.claim: The agent keeps one shared memory across everyone it works with.
claims.quote: The agent keeps one memory across everyone it works with, so what one person explains benefits the whole team.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The People card warns that shared files and chats can appear in responses to users lacking source permissions, regardless of sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: The agent's People card displays this notice: "Any files or chats you share can be summarized and included in the agent's responses to any user, even users without permissions to the files or chats and regardless of sensitivity label."

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Shared memory has no privacy boundary between users.
claims.quote: The agent is guided not to bring up one person's details with someone else, but shared memory has no privacy boundary between users.

claims.claim: Shared memories are deleted after 28 days without anyone interacting with the agent.
claims.quote: If no one interacts with the agent for 28 days, the system automatically deletes its shared memories.

claims.claim: End users cannot opt out of shared memory in this preview.
claims.quote: No. End users can't opt out of shared memory in this preview. By using the agent, you consent to its use of shared memory.

claims.where: controls[3].ui and .api; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No independent UI or API control to disable shared memory is documented; the preview requires turning off agent accounts altogether.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "agent accounts" "shared memory" disable admin API; "Copilot Studio" "agent accounts" "shared memory" sensitivity audience restrict. Opened FAQ and account guide. FAQ: "shared memory can't be turned off independently of agent accounts."

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The agent has its own Microsoft Entra account.
claims.quote: The agent has its own Microsoft Entra account and identity, so admins can govern and audit it like any other identity.

claims.quote: You can view and manage these identities in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

claims.claim: The account does not automatically grant every tool permission.
claims.quote: The agent account does not automatically grant every tool permission. Check which identity a tool uses and grant only the access needed for the job.
